correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern opening and initial northwestward approach
correspondence.finding: The supplied selection begins in the eastern interior and trends northwest. No actually inspected source establishes the chosen initial waterbody, its outlet, or the first through-going stream connection. The model opening is not asserted to be the natural source of Kugaluk River.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper westward interval and possible waterbody transitions
correspondence.finding: The selected upper westward interval was considered, but no readable primary cartography establishes its individual waters, lake entries and exits, or side-stream joins. Broad Kugaluk regional placement does not bridge these connections.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern middle arc and intermediate joins
correspondence.finding: The long middle arc lies within the regional Wollaston study setting. The small-scale location figure and historical landscape overview do not distinguish its actual river/lake succession or intermediate joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle westward continuation and southwestern turn
correspondence.finding: The selected middle continuation and southwestern turn remain without source-to-route correspondence. No nearby lake name or geological landform is assigned to these parts.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward reach and return to a westward course
correspondence.finding: The modeled southward transfer and subsequent westward continuation were considered. The surviving permitted observations do not show the actual connecting channels or identify whether any selected passage traverses lake, wetland, or another waterbody.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower westward corridor and joins
correspondence.finding: NASA prose identifies a Kugaluk River crossing Wollaston Peninsula to Penny Bay, and the original memoir location figure places that named river in the same southwestern regional setting. Neither source establishes these particular selected lower reaches, their feeder junctions, or all intervening through-links.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower southern bend and approach to the coast
correspondence.finding: The final southern bend and western approach require readable corridor material. No observed source resolves the selected passage across the lower coastal setting, and no contemporary tidal condition or channel position is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Final westward reach and selected sea endpoint
correspondence.finding: Penny Bay is the source-supported receiving bay of the regional Kugaluk River. The exact selected terminal reach has not been independently matched to that named outlet at ordinary corridor scale, so even this final connection remains material-pending rather than completed on the strength of regional naming alone.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen southwestern opening
correspondence.finding: The thematic map shows an unnamed tributary approaching the southwestern end of Bluenose Lake from the west. Its mapped western headward continuation does not unambiguously establish the selected initial northeastward opening before the eastward inlet reach. The nearby small waterbodies are not substituted for that opening.

correspondence.component_scope: eastward feeder and southwestern lake entrance
correspondence.finding: The eastward to southeastward unnamed feeder can be followed into the southwestern bay of the large waterbody directly labeled Bluenose Lake. This supports the inlet reach and lake entrance after the unresolved initial opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Bluenose Lake passage and northern outlet
correspondence.finding: The selection traverses the connected southwestern bay and elongate main body of the directly labeled Bluenose Lake, then approaches its narrower northern end. The figure shows the lake outline and its northward outlet connection. The lake name is retained only as a lake-component identity.

correspondence.component_scope: upper outlet river and lake-bearing corridor
correspondence.finding: The map shows a continuous northward outlet watercourse through the small-waterbody surroundings beyond Bluenose Lake, including the transition from the lake-bearing terrain to a more continuous river course. The selected intervening joins follow this mapped corridor; no name is supplied for these river reaches on the inspected figure.

correspondence.component_scope: middle bends and lower northeastward river
correspondence.finding: The characteristic west-returning middle bend, renewed northern course and longer northeastward lower reach agree with the unnamed watercourse shown on the figure. Adjacent eastern drainage and lake strings are distinct from the selected trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The lower watercourse turns northward and visibly reaches the shore of the waterbody labeled Amundsen Gulf. This supports the selected river-to-sea terminal at ordinary corridor scale. No exact active bank, tidal boundary or present distributary is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern Inland Ice opening, regional-sheet edge crossing and initial northward passage
correspondence.finding: The national original covers the complete southern opening and long initial northward part. The regional original begins at its southern neatline within this same part and overlaps the national map northward through ice, marginal exposed-rock terrain and the Hagen Bræ setting. The opening south of that neatline is not attributed to the regional sheet. The full terrain passage, including the map-edge crossing and its continuation to the first join, is accounted for; neither map establishes a continuous natural-river channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Short northern turns across the glacier-margin and Quaternary-covered passage
correspondence.finding: The selected short northward and northwestward parts leave the Hagen Bræ ice setting, pass through the mapped Quaternary-covered margin and exposed-rock belt, and reach the adjacent interior-ice setting south of J. C. Christensen Land. All short joins and the turn into the westward continuation are visible in the original regional cartography. The blue dotted legend unit is undifferentiated Quaternary cover; it is not by itself a mapped lake or a named river.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward middle sequence and its successive short offsets
correspondence.finding: The original regional map accounts for the westward corridor across pale ice terrain bordered by exposed-rock units. The initial margin and all subsequent small bends and joins are visible. No river hydronym is established for these parts, and the modeled line does not turn ice or geological linework into proof of surface or subglacial flow.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern approach and crossing of the intervening rock and Quaternary-covered corridor
correspondence.finding: The northwestern parts approach and cross the narrow exposed-rock and undifferentiated Quaternary-covered passage between the eastern interior-ice setting and the ice within the Academy Land region. The regional original shows the complete intervening terrain and both sides of the crossing. It supports geographic correspondence, without establishing a hydraulic through-link or a shared river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Academy Land ice and exposed-rock approach to the final northward part
correspondence.finding: The remaining northwestern bends and short westward parts pass through the mapped Academy Land ice and adjoining exposed-rock terrain. Their entire course and the join to the last long northward part are covered. Academy Land is a land-region label, and the separate Academy Gletscher to the west is not substituted for a river name on this selected object.

correspondence.component_scope: Final northward land-and-coast passage and actual Independence Fjord endpoint
correspondence.finding: The final selected part runs north from the Academy Land ice-margin setting, across the exposed-rock coastal belt and into the water area labeled Independence Fjord. Both originals expose the actual ending in that fjord, rather than only a nearby land or glacier label. The selected line is not shown to follow a named continuous natural river across the intervening land. Independence Fjord identifies the receiving water setting only; neither a precise contemporary river mouth nor current shoreline and ice-front positions are established.

correspondence.component_scope: western_headward_opening_and_lake_chain
correspondence.finding: The selected opening and its looping western lake-and-stream corridor can be located among the unnamed waters west of Tessik Lake on the Andrew Gordon Bay sheet. The map does not attach a river name to this headward component. This regional match does not resolve the later southern transfer into Kinguk Lake.

correspondence.component_scope: southern_turn_and_transfer_into_kinguk
correspondence.finding: The map depicts the separate lakes and short streams around the selected southern turn west and southwest of Kinguk Lake. It does not establish an unambiguous continuous interpretation of the complete selected transfer from that western lake chain into Kinguk Lake. Nearby water shapes and a common regional setting are insufficient to supply the missing through-link.

correspondence.component_scope: kinguk_ameetuk_and_tessik_inlet
correspondence.finding: The selected northward lake passage corresponds at ordinary scale to Kinguk Lake, Ameetuk Lake and the connecting narrow-water corridor entering the southwestern side of Tessik Lake. These are distinct lake components, not evidence that each water carries the downstream river name.

correspondence.component_scope: tessik_and_angmaluk_transition
correspondence.finding: The eastern and northward selected run is located through Tessik Lake and its northern lake-and-stream continuation toward Angmaluk Lake at the sheet boundary. The map supplies the ordinary lake passages and intervening joins.

correspondence.component_scope: angmaluk_shappa_ashuna
correspondence.finding: The Cory Bay sheet shows the selected northern continuation from Angmaluk Lake through the Shappa Lake corridor into the southeastern part of Ashuna Lake. The larger through-water shapes and their connecting reaches correspond without treating adjacent lakes as a single scalar-named river.

correspondence.component_scope: ashuna_to_kavivau
correspondence.finding: The selected westward and then northward passage corresponds to Ashuna Lake and the narrow northern lake corridor labeled Kavivau Lake on the inspected sheet. Kavivau is retained as that historical map spelling only.

correspondence.component_scope: kommanik_selected_terminal_reach
correspondence.finding: The last selected reaches correspond to the outlet of the Kavivau Lake corridor and the broadened reach labeled Kommanik River. The source continues northwest to Gibson Bay beyond the selected endpoint. It therefore supports the selected downstream river setting, while it does not establish that the selected endpoint itself is the sea mouth.
